Patos Lagoon juvenile fish and environment blocks (PELD-ELPA)

Source: R/elpa.R
elpa_blocks.Rd

Builds two monthly blocks, environment and fish, for one habitat of the Patos Lagoon estuary, southern Brazil, from the PELD-ELPA beach-seine survey (Darwin Core Archive v1.16). The data are licensed CC BY-NC 4.0 and are not shipped with lagprotest: pass a local copy of the archive in path, or leave path = NULL to download it from the SiBBr IPT into the session's temporary directory.

Usage

elpa_blocks(
  habitat = c("estuary", "sandy beach"),
  from = c(1996, 8),
  to = c(2016, 12),
  species = NULL,
  hellinger = TRUE,
  path = NULL
)

Source

Vieira, J. P., Garcia, A. M. and Lemos, V. M. PELD-ELPA: Species composition and abundance patterns of fish assemblages at shallow waters of Patos Lagoon estuary. Version 1.16. Sistema de Informação sobre a Biodiversidade Brasileira (SiBBr), via GBIF, doi:10.15468/kci8zb . Licensed CC BY-NC 4.0: cite the dataset and do not use it commercially. The program is described in Lemos et al. (2022), Earth System Science Data 14: 1015–1041, doi:10.5194/essd-14-1015-2022 .

Arguments

habitat

"estuary" or "sandy beach".

from, to

Integer vectors c(year, month) delimiting the period. The default covers 1996-08 to 2016-12, the longest stretch without unsampled months.

species

Species (scientific names) to keep in the fish block. NULL (default) keeps the most abundant species that together make up 90% of the total catch over all sampling events in the chosen habitat and period; "all" keeps every species.

hellinger

Logical. If TRUE (default), the fish block holds Hellinger-transformed catches, computed on all species before species are selected; if FALSE, mean catch per haul.

path

Path to the archive (.zip) or to a directory with its extracted files. NULL downloads version 1.16 from the SiBBr IPT (about 3 MB), once per session.

Value

A named list of two numeric matrices with one row per month (row names "YYYY-MM"):

Environment

Water temperature (temp, °C), salinity (sal) and Secchi depth (secchi).

Fish

One column per species in species.

Details

Each sampling event is one site in one month, with five seine hauls. Counts are summed by species within an event and divided by five (catch per haul), and both catch and environment are averaged over the sites of the chosen habitat in each month. Months with no record of an environmental variable are filled by linear interpolation; a month with no fish sampling at all is an error, since the blocks must be regular series. No transformation, detrending or deseasonalization is applied to the environment; see the example for the steps used in the lagprotest preprint, which also added freshwater discharge from the Brazilian National Water Agency (not included here).

Examples

if (FALSE) { # interactive()
el <- elpa_blocks("estuary")
detrend <- function(m) apply(m, 2, function(x) residuals(lm(x ~ seq_along(x))))
X <- detrend(log1p(el$Environment))
Y <- detrend(el$Fish)
fit <- lagged_protest(X, Y, lags = 0:6, period = 12, nperm = 999,
                      seed = 1)
fit
}
